 Davion Mitchell 
 MIA 
 Guard

 Davion Mitchell produced 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 10 assists, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 The good news for fantasy managers was that Mitchell recorded a double-double, which included a game-high 10 assists. However, for category-league managers, the six turnovers hurt. Mitchell logged 33 minutes in Wednesday’s opener, with Pelle Larsson (two points, three rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block) taking on the playmaking responsibilities when “Off Night” was on the bench. Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo can also initiate the offense, and they’ll likely need to because Miami lacks depth at point guard. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Pelle Larsson (finger) is available to play against the Hornets on Saturday. 
 Larsson was initially listed as probable, and he has now officially been cleared to suit up. He has played a significant role off the bench this season, though he hasn’t been able to find his shot yet. 
 Pelle Larsson 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Pelle Larsson (finger) is probable for Saturday’s game against the Hornets. 
 Larsson is the only player on the Heat’s injury report. He’s probable with a left finger sprain. Miami figures to be at full strength as they look for their first win of the season against the Hornets. 
 Bam Adebayo 
 MIA 
 Center-Forward 
 #13 
 Bam Adebayo (groin) and Pelle Larsson (illness) participated in Sunday’s practice. 
 Neither Adebayo nor Larsson played in the Heat’s final two preseason games, but both are on track to play in Wednesday’s regular-season opener against the Timberwolves. Adebayo’s status matters more to the Heat and fantasy managers because of his role in the rotation. As for Larsson, he’ll provide added perimeter depth off the bench. 
 Davion Mitchell 
 BKN 
 Forward 
 #17 
 Davion Mitchell had 13 Points, (4-of-8 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, two steals and a 3-pointer on Wednesday. 
 Davion showed how much of a pest he is defensively in this game with his full court pressure and defensive numbers. He did leave the game temporarily after hitting his head on Day’Ron Sharpe’s knee, but he returned to the game. He should be primed to at worst, be a steals and assists streamer for redraft leagues. 
 Bam Adebayo 
 MIA 
 Center-Forward 
 #13 
 Bam Adebayo (groin), Pelle Larsson (illness) and Dru Smith (calf) are out for Wednesday’s exhibition against the Nets. 
 Adebayo is dealing with right groin tightness, and his absence frees up additional minutes for Nick Richards. With his contract for the upcoming season not being guaranteed unless he makes the Opening Night roster, this is a big opportunity for Richards. With Klay Thompson available, he’ll slide into the starting lineup spot Larsson occupied in Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves. Smith’s absence won’t change anything regarding fantasy basketball, as starting point guard Davion Mitchell is available. 
 Pelle Larsson 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Pelle Larsson (illness) will not return to Saturday’s exhibition against the Timberwolves. 
 Larsson has been dealing with an illness for a few days, but it did not keep the Heat wing from starting Saturday’s game. He logged 25 minutes, finishing with 14 points (4-of-15 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), three rebounds and five assists. With Miami’s lack of perimeter depth, Larsson will have more opportunities to contribute this season. For that reason, he’s worth considering as a late-round option in deeper leagues. 
 Pelle Larsson 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Pelle Larsson accumulated 13 points (3-of-3 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), two rebounds, two assists and two steals in Saturday’s exhibition against the Raptors. 
 Having agreed to a four-year extension last month, Larsson’s immediate future in Miami is secure. He came off the bench on Saturday and took on more playmaking responsibilities because of the Heat’s lack of depth at point guard. With Dru Smith (hamstring) currently out and not guaranteed to be a full go when the regular season begins, Larsson is even more enticing as a late-round option. 
 Davion Mitchell 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Davion Mitchell notched three points (1-of-5 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s exhibition against the Raptors. 
 Like the other Heat starters, Mitchell was shut down at the half. He didn’t have a great night shooting, but that shouldn’t dissuade fantasy managers from selecting “Off Night” in drafts. Miami lacks depth at point guard, especially with Dru Smith (hamstring) not guaranteed to be fully ready when the regular season begins. With Giannis Antetokounmpo joining the lineup, Mitchell could potentially provide more value in assists and three-pointers than he did in 2025-26. 
 Dru Smith 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #12 
 According to Ira Winderman of the Sun-Sentinel, Dru Smith (calf) is out for “a couple of weeks.” 
 Smith, who played a career-high 70 games last season, is dealing with a strained right calf. With the reported timeline, he may be limited when the regular season begins. Smith’s absence doesn’t affect fantasy basketball, but it does leave a Heat team already light on options at point guard down a rotation piece. Starter Davion Mitchell has become more important, especially if Smith isn’t ready when the regular season begins. 
 Pelle Larsson 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #9 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Pelle Larsson has agreed to a four-year, $60 million contract extension with the Heat. 
 Larsson carved out a solid role for the Heat last season, starting 54 of the 70 regular-season games and averaging 11.4 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game overall. He should again be a part of the nightly rotation in his third NBA season for a Miami team that expects to have a much higher ceiling with the offseason acquisition of Giannis Antetokounmpo. From a fantasy perspective, Larsson could take another leap in production and build in 2026-27 on a strong end to his second season.
